mechanism_narrative: A higher level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS exceeds its 1-year moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk aversion and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals an economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate investment and earnings forecasts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines by >1% and UNRATE rises by >0.2% over the past month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by strong GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an imminent economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100 during a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%).

mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces discount rates for equity valuation, increasing present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting monetary tightening expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a rise in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a shift toward non-housing consumer spending, supporting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines by >1% and RSAFS rises by >0.5% over the past month.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 3.5%), a deceleration in employment growth (PAYEMS) signals weakening economic momentum, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate hiring slows and earnings growth falters.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth rate falls below 0.1% and UNRATE is below 3.5%.
